cornflower.note: Default accent only. The user replaces this in Settings; never treat it as a fixed brand color.

dusty-rose.note: Default petal color. A separate user setting from the accent, and required to stay visually distinct from it.

on-accent-inverse.note: Label color on an accent fill when the accent's luminance is at or below 0.55. Above it, Midnight Graphite is used instead.

display.purpose: Life tracker and full-canvas moments only. Absent from ordinary task UI.

headline.purpose: Page-level headings on analytics and finance surfaces.

title.purpose: App bar titles, dialog titles, list-tile titles, section headers.

body.purpose: Journal and dream entry text, menu items, dialog content, snackbars. Reading and choosing share a size.

label.purpose: Buttons, pills, chips, field labels, nav rail labels. The only role above weight 400 by default.

shadows.name: hairline-light
shadows.purpose: The primary separation tool on cream. Reach for this before reaching for a shadow.

shadows.name: hairline-dark
shadows.purpose: Same role on the dark theme.

shadows.name: subtle-light
shadows.purpose: Small floating elements on cream — menu-item hover lift, chips, drag proxies. 24px base blur is not used here; small elements use ~4px base, scaled 2.2x.

shadows.name: subtle-dark
shadows.purpose: Same role on dark, at native blur.

shadows.name: surface-light
shadows.purpose: Large floating surfaces on cream — menus, popovers, dialogs, modals. 24px base blur multiplied by the 2.2x light-theme blur scale.

shadows.name: surface-dark
shadows.purpose: Same role on dark, at native 1.0x blur.

shadows.name: focus-glow-glass
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on the glass button only. Uses the live accent at 50% alpha with a 1px spread.

motion.name: control-feedback
motion.purpose: Button overlay and rail item state changes. The fastest tier.

motion.name: house-transition
motion.purpose: The default transition, used ~20x across the codebase. When in doubt, this one.

motion.name: traverse
motion.purpose: Reserved for elements that actually move across space.

motion.name: ease-mark
motion.purpose: easeOutBack — reserved for the checkbox mark. The system's only overshoot in core controls.

components.name: Filled Button
components.description: The primary action. Accent fill, borrowed-contrast label, no ripple.
components.css: .ds-btn-filled { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1px; color: #FFFFFF; background-color: #7C9EFF; background-image: none; border: none; border-radius: 18px; padding: 12px 20px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.03); transition: background-image 90ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), box-shadow 90ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-btn-filled:hover { background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08)); box-shadow: 0 2px 7px rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.03); } .ds-btn-filled:focus-visible { outline: none; background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08)); box-shadow: 0 2px 7px rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.03); } .ds-btn-filled:active { background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.16), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.16)); box-shadow: none; }

components.name: Outlined Button
components.description: Secondary action. A blended-line edge that steps to the accent line on interaction.
components.css: .ds-btn-outlined { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1px; color: #2B303B; background-color: transparent; background-image: none; border: 1px solid rgba(150, 172, 224, 0.38); border-radius: 18px; padding: 12px 20px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 90ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), background-image 90ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-btn-outlined:hover { border-color: rgba(150, 172, 224, 0.55); background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08)); } .ds-btn-outlined:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: rgba(150, 172, 224, 0.55); background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08)); } .ds-btn-outlined:active { background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.16), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.16)); }

components.name: Text Button
components.description: Tertiary action. Compact density, shrink-wrapped tap target, 40px minimum height.
components.css: .ds-btn-text { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1px; color: #2B303B; background-color: transparent; background-image: none; border: none; border-radius: 18px; padding: 12px 16px; min-height: 40px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-image 90ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-btn-text:hover { background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08)); } .ds-btn-text:focus-visible { outline: none; background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08)); } .ds-btn-text:active { background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.16), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.16)); }

components.name: Glass Button
components.description: The signature control and the system's one licensed piece of ornament on an interactive element. Backdrop blur under a diagonal fill gradient, a specular edge stroke, and a top gloss reflection.
components.css: .ds-btn-glass { position: relative; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.2px; color: #2B303B; padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.35); border-radius: 12px; cursor: pointer; overflow: hidden; isolation: isolate; -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.07) 0%, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.06) 50%, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.03) 100%); box-shadow: 0 2px 13px rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.12), inset 1px 1px 0 rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.22), inset -1px -1px 0 rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.09); transition: transform 100ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), box-shadow 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), background-image 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-btn-glass::before { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; height: 18px; pointer-events: none; border-radius: 12px 12px 0 0; background-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.06), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0)); transition: background-image 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-btn-glass:hover { background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.086) 0%, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.075) 50%, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.038) 100%); box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.25), inset 1.5px 1.5px 0 rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.29), inset -1.5px -1.5px 0 rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.12); } .ds-btn-glass:hover::before { background-image: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.14), rgba(43, 48, 59, 0)); } .ds-btn-glass:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.25), 0 0 18px 1px rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.5), inset 1.5px 1.5px 0 rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.29); } .ds-btn-glass:active { transform: scale(0.96); background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.095) 0%, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.084) 50%, rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.042) 100%); }

components.name: Notched Text Field
components.description: The floating label cuts a gap in the border stroke rather than sitting on a filled chip. Focus steps the stroke to 1.8px in the accent at 95% alpha.
components.html: <fieldset class='ds-field'><legend class='ds-field-label'>Entry title</legend><input class='ds-field-input' type='text' value='Tuesday, and the rain finally stopped' /></fieldset>
components.css: .ds-field { position: relative; margin: 0; padding: 0 16px 18px; background-color: #FFFEFA; border: 1px solid rgba(150, 172, 224, 0.38); border-radius: 14px; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), border-width 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-field-label { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1px; color: #2B303B; padding: 0 6px; margin-left: -6px; transition: color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-field-input { display: block; width: 100%; padding: 8px 0 0; font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.5px; line-height: 1.5; color: #2B303B; background: transparent; border: none; caret-color: #7C9EFF; } .ds-field-input:focus { outline: none; } .ds-field:focus-within { border-color: rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.95); border-width: 1.8px; } .ds-field:focus-within .ds-field-label { color: #7C9EFF; }

components.name: Selector Pill (active)
components.description: The compact toolbar control. Activation is signalled by a 1px accent edge, never by a fill change.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1px; color: #2B303B; background-color: rgba(240, 235, 226, 0.5); border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 12px; padding: 6px 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-pill:hover { background-color: rgba(240, 235, 226, 0.75); } .ds-pill:focus-visible { outline: none; background-color: rgba(240, 235, 226, 0.75); } .ds-pill-active { border-color: #7C9EFF; }

components.name: Menu Surface
components.description: Zero Material elevation, transparent Material shadow, a 1px accent edge, and zero padding so items reach the surface edge. Item highlights clip to the menu's own corner geometry.
components.css: .ds-menu { display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 200px; background-color: #FDFBF6; border: 1px solid #7C9EFF; border-radius: 18px; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; box-shadow: 0 8px 53px rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.05); } .ds-menu-item { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.5px; text-align: left; color: #2B303B; background-color: transparent; border: none; padding: 12px 12px; cursor: pointer; border-radius: 0; transition: background-color 90ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-menu-item:hover { background-color: rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08); } .ds-menu-item:focus-visible { outline: none; background-color: rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08); } .ds-menu-item-first { border-radius: 18px 18px 0 0; } .ds-menu-item-last { border-radius: 0 0 18px 18px; }

components.name: Nav Rail Item (selected)
components.description: The only global navigation. Selection is signalled by surface and border, never by a type-weight change.
components.css: .ds-rail-item { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; width: 68px; padding: 10px 0; font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: #2B303B; background-color: transparent; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 18px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 120ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), border-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-rail-item:hover { background-color: rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08); } .ds-rail-item:focus-visible { outline: none; background-color: rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.08); } .ds-rail-item-selected { background-color: rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.10); border-color: rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.55); }

components.name: Checkbox (checked)
components.description: Hand-painted on a 14x14 canvas with a 2px-radius fill — the sharpest corner in the system. The tick uses easeOutBack, the only overshoot in the core controls, spent here because checking something off is the most-repeated satisfying act in the app.
components.css: .ds-check { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.5px; color: #2B303B; cursor: pointer; } .ds-check input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 0; height: 0; } .ds-check-box { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 14px; height: 14px; border: 1px solid rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.5); border-radius: 2px; background-color: transparent; transition: background-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1), border-color 200ms cubic-bezier(0.215, 0.61, 0.355, 1); } .ds-check-box svg { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.4); transition: opacity 110ms linear, transform 200ms cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); } .ds-check input:checked + .ds-check-box { background-color: #7C9EFF; border-color: #7C9EFF; } .ds-check input:checked + .ds-check-box svg { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); } .ds-check input:focus-visible + .ds-check-box { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(124, 158, 255, 0.3); }

components.name: Card Surface
components.description: Cards carry an edge, not just a shadow. The border does the separating; the shadow only lifts it off the paper.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; min-width: 200px; padding: 16px; background-color: #FDFBF6; border: 1px solid rgba(150, 172, 224, 0.26); border-radius: 18px; box-shadow: 0 8px 53px rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.05); } .ds-card-title { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.1px; color: #2B303B; } .ds-card-value { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 36px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.22; color: #2B303B; } .ds-card-meta { font-family: IosevkaAile, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.4px; color: rgba(43, 48, 59, 0.55); }

narrative.overview:
Voyager is built from two materials held in tension. The surface you write on is warm and physical — a cream paper stock with real grain, petals drifting down across it, everything matte and flat as if it were printed rather than rendered. The tools you write with are exact: Iosevka Aile, one-pixel hairlines, tight radii, no ripple, state changes measured in tens of milliseconds. Neither material wins. The contrast between them is the identity, and the fastest way to break this system is to soften a control to make it feel friendlier, or to sharpen the canvas to make it feel more serious.

The practical consequence is a strict division of labor. Ornament belongs to the canvas layer and nowhere else. The paper grain, the falling petals, the watercolor life tree, the dark theme's triangle grid — these are permitted to be lush because they sit behind the work. A dropdown, a text field, a list row gets none of it. Controls are instrument-side: they hold an edge, respond immediately, and get out of the way. This is why the light palette's four surface tones step only a few points of luminance apart. Wide steps would reintroduce the layered, floating look that the paper texture exists to replace.

The system is calm, precise, and warm — in that order of priority when they conflict. Calm means nothing moves that wasn't asked to move. Precise means a hairline stays a hairline even when the theme goes pale; the light theme raises its outline alpha rather than let borders dissolve. Warm means the warmth is earned from material, not from rounded corners or encouraging language. Stock Material 3 is the confirmed anti-reference: no tonal elevation surfaces, no filled-tonal buttons, no FABs, no ripple splashes. Voyager runs on Material's machinery but rejects its appearance, and the theme enforces this at the root with NoSplash.splashFactory, zero-elevation menus, and transparent surface tints.
keyCharacteristics: Two complete backgrounds, not one inverted: cream paper with petals in light, an accent-tinted triangle-grid shader in dark
A single user-chosen accent color that every surface derives from — no fixed brand hue
Flat and matte by doctrine; shadows at 3–5% opacity in light, spread 2.2× wider to compensate
Iosevka Aile everywhere, including body copy — the instrument register applied to prose
Hairlines and outlines derived from the accent, not from black or white
Motion in the 90–150 ms band, easeOutCubic, with celebration reserved for real milestones

rules.name: The Blended Line Rule
rules.body: Hairlines and outlines are never the raw accent and never raw black or white. The accent is first lerped toward the theme's line target — white on dark at 42%, Ink Slate on light at 30% — and only then given an alpha (26% for dividers, 38% for outlines in light; 24% / 34% in dark). This is what keeps a line legible whichever direction the theme runs, and why the light theme needs less blending but more alpha.

rules.name: The Borrowed Contrast Rule
rules.body: Text sitting on an accent-colored fill picks its color from the accent's own luminance, not from the theme. Above 0.55 luminance it takes Midnight Graphite; below, white. A pale accent needs dark text in both themes, so the theme cannot be the input.

rules.name: The Dark Scrim Rule
rules.body: Modal barriers stay black-based in both themes (55% dark, 28% light). A light scrim over cream is indistinguishable from the page and stops reading as "behind a modal."

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Iosevka Aile is the typeface of the product, not a default. Never introduce a second family for headings, code, numerals, or "personality." Contrast comes from weight, size, and case — never from a face change.

rules.name: The Inherited Scale Rule
rules.body: Type roles resolve from the theme's TextTheme. Never hand-set a fontSize on a widget when a role already fits; reach for AppFonts.style() only when building something the scale genuinely does not cover.

rules.name: The Blur-Not-Black Rule
rules.body: To make a light-theme shadow read, widen the blur. Never raise the opacity past 5%. VoyagerColors.shadowBlurScale exists to be multiplied into every blur radius — a hand-written BoxShadow that ignores it will look correct in dark and wrong in light.

rules.name: The Grime Rule
rules.body: Never let a shadow default to black. Read VoyagerColors.shadow, which resolves to Ink Slate on cream.

dos: Do derive every line color through Color.lerp(accent, lineTarget, lineAmount) and then alpha it. The Blended Line Rule is what makes a user-chosen accent safe at any luminance.

Do read semantic colors from VoyagerColors.of(context) — hairline, strongHairline, scrim, shadow, chartGrid, highlightWash, onAccent. Each one exists because the naive value (Colors.white at 10%, black shadow, white highlight) fails in one theme.
Do multiply every blur radius by shadowBlurScale.
Do blend toward highlightWash to make something read as lifted — white on dark, Ink Slate on light.
Do keep the four surface tones tightly stepped. If a surface needs to read as more forward, give it a hairline, not a bigger luminance jump.
Do put new icons in VoyagerIcons rather than referencing Phosphor sets directly.
Do let backgrounds animate on their own timers, decoupled from the app's frame pipeline.
Do test every new surface in both themes before calling it finished. They are two designed worlds, not a palette swap.
donts: Don't reintroduce Material 3's stock appearance — tonal elevation surfaces, filled-tonal buttons, FABs, or ripple splashes. This is the confirmed anti-reference.
Don't hardcode the accent or any brand hue. The accent and petal colors are user settings; a literal #7C9EFF anywhere outside the theme's default parameter is a bug.
Don't rely on the accent alone to carry meaning. It can be set to any hue at any luminance, so state must also be signalled by shape, position, weight, or an edge.
Don't raise a light-theme shadow above 5% opacity. Widen the blur instead.
Don't let a shadow default to Material's black on the cream theme.
Don't introduce a second typeface, for any purpose.
Don't hand-set fontSize where a type role already fits.
Don't add ornament to controls. Decoration lives on the canvas layer — paper grain, petals, the triangle grid, the life tree — and the glass button is the one deliberate exception, already spent.
Don't let a page paint its own opaque scaffold fill. Content composes over the background pipeline; opaque panels break the paper.
Don't spend celebration motion on routine actions. easeOutBack and confetti are reserved for genuine milestones; everything else resolves in 90–150 ms without a bounce.
